newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delay EMU if rules not met - German SPD.
newsitem.headline: Delay EMU if rules not met - German SPD.

text.p: European monetary union should be delayed if Germay does not meet the convergence criteria, Heinz Schleusser, Social Democrat (SPD) finance minister of North Rhine-Westphalia, said on Saturday.

"The stability of the euro is more important than the schedule for introducing it. The citizens must have trust in the new European currency," Schleusser said in an interview with Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

His remarks echoed recent comments by German eurosceptics from opposite political camps: Gerhard Schroeder, SPD premier of Lower Saxony, and Edmund Stoiber, the Christian Social Union's premier of Bavaria.
Germans must be convinced they are not trading in their trusty marks for a softer currency, so that they do not fear losing the assets they have built up over a lifetime, Schleusser said.
"In this situation, a discussion of a delay has nothing to do with euroscepticism," Schleusser said, adding he doubted Germany could meet the debt and budget deficit criteria in 1997 or even in 1998.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel is expected to announce next week a supplementary budget with a larger deficit, but coalition sources said it would still be in line with efforts to meet the Maastricht criteria.
